messages:
carol: Heads-up: alert from retention job — ~48 DB snapshot objects moved to Glacier-Deep Archive without our CMEK metadata on transition. Likely lifecycle rule fired on objects missing tag `cmek:present=true`.
tom: Where were they moved from? bucket `redwood-db-snapshots-prod`?
carol: yes. Keys like snapshots/tenant-12/2026-04-10/db-snap-0001.sql.gz. `aws s3api head-object` shows no `x-redwood-cmek-id`.
yash: timeline: we rolled out a tagging-enforcer in the uploader two weeks ago; there was a rollback during last night's deploy. Could be that rollback dropped tags on in-flight multipart uploads.
leah: if objects are in Glacier Deep Archive we can still restore but it takes hours and costs more. Also compliance requires CMEK for some tenants.
carol: encops-bot, open incident for encryption + retention.
encops-bot: incident created INC-2026-0602. Triage channel: #inc-INC-2026-0602. Tags: encryption, s3, glacier, retention.
ton: immediate mitigation: suspend lifecycle transition rules for the affected prefix to stop further moves. I've queued a change to exclude `snapshots/` prefix until we fix.
yash: RBAC check: did we recently rename the `backup-uploader` role? I recall a service-account rename in infra-PR #456 that moved from `backup-uploader-v1` to `backup-uploader`. That might have lost kms:Decrypt grants for the re-encrypt runner.
leah: I checked CloudTrail: several `kms:Decrypt` failures from our rehydration job at 1738999000, matching the same objects. Looks like the runner SA didn't have `kms:Decrypt`.
carol: plan: 1) suspend lifecycle transitions (tom) 2) create an IAM/KMS grant for reencrypt-runner (leah) 3) restore Glacier objects to S3 Standard (oncall / ops) 4) reupload or re-encrypt objects with CMEK tag preserving original keys 5) add a pre-transition audit that checks CMEK present and fails otherwise.
leah: creating grant now: `aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-backups --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/reencrypt-runner --operations Encrypt,Decrypt --name grant-reencrypt` . Will add grant to incident log.
oncall: starting restore job for 48 objects using expedited where possible, estimating restores finish in ~2h.
tom: lifecycle rule suspended at 1739000210. No new transitions observed.
yash: reencrypt runner permissions patched at 1739000305. KMS audit shows Decrypts succeeding after that.
carol: re-encrypt approach: download, run `aws s3 cp` then `aws s3 cp --metadata x-redwood-cmek-id=...` to preserve CMK metadata. We'll batch and parallelize tenant-by-tenant.
leah: also adding a post-commit test in uploader that asserts `x-redwood-cmek-id` present on head-object for sample uploads. Opening SEC-910 for that.
encops-bot: update: restores in-flight; re-encrypt queued; monitoring for any new missing-metadata transitions.
carol: follow-ups: OP-350 (lifecycle precheck), SEC-911 (RBAC playbook for service-account renames), COMPL-44 (customer notification draft if any consumer data impacted).
carol: summary: root cause = uploader/rollback edgecase stripped CMEK metadata during multipart finalization; contributing factor = recent SA rename removed a grant for the reencrypt runner. Both needed to align to cause objects to transition unprotected to Glacier. Postmortem to follow.
